newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African tax amnesty nets about one billion rand.
newsitem.headline: S.African tax amnesty nets about one billion rand.

text.p: The tax amnesty that ended in February is likely to net around one billion rand and to expand the tax base, South African Revenue Services chief executive Piet Liebenberg told legislators on Monday.

Liebenberg said that with applications still being processed, the total stood at 24,616 new registrations on March 1, netting 966.3 million rand in back taxes and leading to 887 million in interest and penalties being written off.
The tax amnesty allowed people coming into the system to clear taxes owing since South Africa's transition to democracy in 1994 without having to pay penalties or interest.
Liebenberg, who heads a newly revamped revenue service, said the response to the amnesty had been disappointing, but that it had helped to raise awareness of the issue.
"Statistically, we have not had the sort of response we would have liked to see, but on balance we have raised the level of awarenss quite remarkably.

"We have invested in direct and indirect expenses something in the order of 10 million rand in cash in this programme. It looks as if we will, by the end of this month, be able to collect probably something in the order of one billion (rand) out of the programme," he said.
